body.statement:
Let \(q_d=\min\{1/4,(d-4)/[2(d-2)]\}\), and let \(U_{N,K}\) and \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\) be defined in Definition~\texttt{def:plugin-lower-bound}. For fixed \(d>4\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1/4)\),
\[
B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\in\mathcal H_\alpha
\]
and there are constants \(0<c_{d,\alpha}\le C_{d,\alpha}<\infty\) such that
\[
c_{d,\alpha}N^{-1/2}
\le E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)
\le C_{d,\alpha}\left[N^{-1/2}+\min\left\{\frac r{K^2},\frac1K m^{-2/d}\right\}\right].
\]
Consequently \(E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\asymp N^{-1/2}\) uniformly along every legal array satisfying \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\); here \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\). No matching nonparametric expected-length converse is asserted for smaller \(K\).
body.proof_tex:
Let
\[
U_{N,K}=C_d\left[N^{-1/2}+\min\left\{\frac r{K^2},\frac1K m^{-2/d}\right\}\right],
\qquad u_{N,K}=\frac{U_{N,K}}{\alpha},
\]
where \(C_d\) is chosen so that Theorem~\texttt{thm:improved-plugin-upper} yields
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P}\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}|\widehat L-L(\mathbf P)|\le U_{N,K}.
\tag{7}
\]
The quantity \(U_{N,K}\) is strictly positive because \(C_d>0\) and \(N^{-1/2}>0\). For every nonnegative \(Y\) and positive \(u\), the pointwise inequality \(\mathbf 1\{Y>u\}\le Y/u\) gives \(\Pr(Y>u)\le\mathbb EY/u\) after integration. Applying this derived inequality with \(Y=|\widehat L-L(\mathbf P)|\) and then using (7) gives, for every \(\mathbf P\),
\[
\Pr_{\mathbf P}\left\{|\widehat L-L(\mathbf P)|>u_{N,K}\right\}
\le \frac{\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}|\widehat L-L(\mathbf P)|}{u_{N,K}}
\le\alpha.
\tag{8}
\]
On the complementary event, \(\widehat L-u_{N,K}\le L(\mathbf P)\). The squared-sum cost is nonnegative, so its infimum satisfies \(L(\mathbf P)\ge0\). Consequently
\[
B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}
=\max\{0,\widehat L-u_{N,K}\}
\le L(\mathbf P)
\tag{9}
\]
on that event. Equations (8)--(9) imply
\[
\inf_{\mathbf P}\Pr_{\mathbf P}\{B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\le L(\mathbf P)\}\ge1-\alpha,
\]
which is exactly \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\in\mathcal H_\alpha\) by Definition~\texttt{def:honest-bounds}.

For length, the definition of the maximum gives \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\ge\widehat L-u_{N,K}\). Hence, pointwise,
\[
\begin{aligned}
[L(\mathbf P)-B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}]_+
&\le[L(\mathbf P)-\widehat L+u_{N,K}]_+\\
&\le|L(\mathbf P)-\widehat L|+u_{N,K}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking expectations and using (7) yields
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P}\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}[(L(\mathbf P)-B_N^{\mathrm{plug}})_+]
\le(1+\alpha^{-1})U_{N,K}.
\tag{10}
\]
Since Definition~\texttt{def:minimax-excess-length} takes the infimum over all honest lower bounds and (9) proves that this particular bound is honest, (10) proves the asserted upper bound after absorbing \(1+\alpha^{-1}\) into \(C_{d,\alpha}\).

For the converse, take the ordered pair in Lemma~\texttt{lem:bernoulli-two-point}. With the notation of (2), \(L_1-L_0=\Delta\ge aN^{-1/2}\) and \(\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb P_0,\mathbb P_1)\le1/4\). Let \(B_N\in\mathcal H_\alpha\) be arbitrary. Honesty at the low-endpoint law and the defining total-variation inequality imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_1(B_N\le L_0)
&\ge \mathbb P_0(B_N\le L_0)-\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb P_0,\mathbb P_1)\\
&\ge1-\alpha-\frac14>\frac12,
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
where the strict final inequality uses the declared condition \(\alpha<1/4\). On \(\{B_N\le L_0\}\),
\[
[L_1-B_N]_+\ge L_1-L_0=\Delta.
\]
Thus (11) gives
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P}\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}[(L(\mathbf P)-B_N)_+]
\ge\mathbb E_1[(L_1-B_N)_+]
\ge\frac{a}{2}N^{-1/2}.
\tag{12}
\]
Taking the infimum over \(B_N\in\mathcal H_\alpha\) proves the lower bound.

Finally, use \(m=N/K\). If \(d=5\), then \(q_d=1/6\), and \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\) gives
\[
K^{-1}m^{-2/d}=N^{-2/d}K^{-(d-2)/d}
\le c_0^{-(d-2)/d}N^{-1/2}.
\]
If \(d\ge6\), then \(q_d=1/4\), and \(r\le d\) gives
\[
r/K^2\le dc_0^{-2}N^{-1/2}.
\]
Thus in either dimension regime the minimum in \(U_{N,K}\) is \(O_d(N^{-1/2})\) whenever \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\). Combining this calculation with (10) and (12) proves the root-\(N\) conclusion. Because (12) uses only the Bernoulli pair, it proves no smaller-arm nonparametric converse, as the statement explicitly records.
body.justification: Markov calibration of the uniform mean plug-in error proves coverage, and the same allowance bounds expected excess length.
body.gap: The ordered Bernoulli pair proves only the root-\(N\) converse; a smaller-arm nonparametric one-sided converse remains open.
body.consumer: It gives a reportable honest endpoint with sampling conservatism matched in the root-\(N\) region.
